facts.text: It has metallic golden or coppery green upperparts, white cheeks, and white underparts barred with dark green.
facts.quote: It has metallic golden or coppery green upperparts and white cheeks and underparts barred with dark green.

facts.text: The shining bronze cuckoo is hard to spot but easier to hear.
facts.quote: Hard to spot and easier to hear, the shining bronze cuckoo is 13–18 cm (5.1–7.1 in) in overall length

facts.text: A female lays a single egg in a host's nest and removes one of the host's eggs; the cuckoo chick then ejects the host nestlings.
facts.quote: A female shining bronze cuckoo lays a single egg in a host nest and removes a host egg.  After hatching, the baby cuckoo ejects the host nestlings from the nest.

facts.text: In a Kaikōura study, the cuckoos heavily parasitised the second broods of grey warblers, targeting 55% of nests.
facts.quote: the shining bronze cuckoos missing the first but parasitising heavily the second broods of the season (55% of nests in a study in Kaikōura)

facts.text: It eats caterpillars and beetles that other birds avoid, including magpie moth caterpillars and ladybirds.
facts.quote: the shining bronze cuckoo eats insects that are avoided by other birds, such as caterpillars, particularly those of the magpie moth, and beetles, particularly ladybirds

facts.text: Its gizzard catches caterpillar spines in a soft thick lining, and the spines are spat back out by the bird.
facts.quote: The shining bronze cuckoo's gizzard is lined with a soft thick lining which catches the caterpillar spines; these fall away and are spat out by the bird.

facts.text: A young cuckoo has been heard imitating the alarm call of baby chestnut-rumped heathwrens, one of its occasional hosts.
facts.quote: a pair of chestnut-rumped heathwren was encountered with a juvenile shining bronze cuckoo which imitated the alarm call of a baby heathwren

facts.text: It is the most southerly ranging brood parasitic bird species in the world, extending to at least 46°S in New Zealand.
facts.quote: It may also parasitise other Acanthizidae species, and is also the most southerly ranging brood parasitic bird species in the world, extending to at least 46°S in New Zealand.

facts.text: The shining bronze cuckoo is found in Australia, Indonesia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu.
facts.quote: a species of cuckoo in the family Cuculidae, found in Australia, Indonesia, New Caledonia, New Zealand, Papua New Guinea, Solomon Islands, and Vanuatu

facts.text: New Zealand populations winter in the Solomon Islands and arrive back in New Zealand from mid August.
facts.quote: New Zealand populations winter in the Solomon Islands and arrive in New Zealand from mid August
